newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone rebel chief snubs U.N. team.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief snubs U.N. team.

text.p: Sierra Leone's rebel leader Foday Sankoh refused to hold talks with a United Nations mission on Friday, objecting to the presence of U.N. envoy Berhanu Dinka.

The talks in Ivory Coast were part of the U.N.'s assessment of Sierra Leone's peacekeeping needs after the government and rebels signed an accord on November 30 ending more than five years of civil war.

"Dinka is an obstacle to peace in Sierra Leone. The U.N. is aware of it because I have complained on several occasions about his partisanship in my country," Sankoh said, with Dinka sitting by his side at the meeting at Sankoh's Abidjan residence.
The U.N. officials packed their bags and left after trying in vain for two hours to convince Sankoh that talks could not take place without the representative of the Security Council.

Dinka, the U.N. special envoy in Sierra Leone, told reporters who watched the drama that Sankoh was angry because he had refused to give U.N. cash to the guerrilla chief without accounting for it. Sankoh vehemently denied this in a radio interview later.
Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front rebels took up arms in 1991. The guerrilla leader has lived in Abidjan since leaving his jungle hideout in March for talks in Ivory Coast.
The Ivorian government brokered talks that led to the accord ending the war that has killed at least 10,000 people, according to official estimates.
The two-member U.N. mission held talks with Sierra Leone's President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah in the capital Freetown last week and visited key provincial towns to assess peacekeeping needs.
The team was scheduled to return to New York on Monday.
